reviews.rationale: Selected SEC exhibit rows show a broad sequential softening: every disclosed GAAP revenue component and total revenue declined, operating and pretax income fell, and both GAAP and company-defined non-GAAP net income declined, so the weakness is not confined to one accounting basis. Operating cash flow and company-defined free cash flow also fell, and other expense, net became a larger drag, while cost of revenues and R&D rose and SG&A fell. A restructuring charge appears only in the event-period extract with no baseline comparator, so its contribution cannot be measured here. The thesis is a source-bounded baseline with no stated assumptions, catalysts or invalidation conditions, and the extract contains no guidance, no year-over-year comparison, no segment or volume/pricing detail, and no explanation of the drivers behind the revenue decline or the expense mix shift. Because the stored thesis lacks the assumption structure needed to judge whether this sequential pattern confirms or breaks the research case, the review is held for clarification rather than upgraded, downgraded or invalidated; conviction and status are preserved and the thesis remains blocked from downstream decisions pending a sourced, complete, conflict-free follow-up.

Because the non-GAAP measure also fell, the softening is not merely an artifact of the reconciliation items, and the cash-flow rows point the same way, so the operating engine looks weaker on both an accrual and a cash basis. The practical implication for the research state is that the stored thesis, which is only a source-bounded baseline with no stated assumptions, catalysts or invalidation conditions, cannot yet be judged confirmed or broken; the appropriate posture is a preserved research hold pending a thesis with explicit testable assumptions and a fuller filing-based explanation.","counterevidence":"Several selected rows cut against a simple margin-collapse story: selling, general and administrative expense was lower, which partially offsets the higher cost of revenues and research and development in the total operating expense line, and the income tax provision was lower, which cushioned the decline from pretax to net income rather than amplifying it. The company-defined share-based compensation add-back and the excess tax benefit adjustment also moved in directions that make the non-GAAP bridge less generous than the baseline, so part of the non-GAAP decline reflects a changing reconciliation rather than only operating performance. These are opposing indications, not proof of resilience, and none of them establishes a cause.","uncertainty":"All comparisons are sequential displayed-value arithmetic between two selected quarterly exhibits, not year-over-year trends, and the extract contains no guidance, no consensus context, no segment volume or pricing detail, no revenue-recognition or contract-timing disclosure, and no management explanation of the revenue decline or the expense mix shift. A restructuring charge appears only in the event-period extract with no baseline comparator, so its contribution to the expense and cash-flow movements cannot be measured here, and its absence from the baseline extract does not establish that no comparable charge existed in the earlier period. Other expense, net is a signed residual whose composition is not disclosed in these rows. The thesis itself lacks assumptions, catalysts and invalidation conditions, which is the main reason the review is held rather than re-rated. Evidence that would change the view includes a full filing with segment and driver disclosure, year-over-year comparators, guidance versus realized results, and a restated or clarified baseline that makes the restructuring and other-expense items comparable across periods.","asserted_state":{"review_id":"tr_dd68008a042445a89dc8","evidence_ids":["RS-FICO-Q2","RS-FICO-Q3"],"next_review_at":"2026-11-30T00:00:00Z","decision_hold":true,"actionability":"blocked","alert_status":"acknowledged"}}}
